lines.text: How could the words: "forgetting what lies behind and
straining forward" be appropriate in such a case? Does
not such a man find it easier to turn away from his past?
Has not the temptation of self-complacency been spared
him? No, he has encountered it in a far more dangerous
guise. Precisely such a judgment about his past, a judgment
made in the bitterness of disillusionment or despair, in a far
more sinister way fetters a man to his past, to himself and
to the old Adam. Such a one is tempted to cling tenaciously
to his disillusionment, his bitterness, his self-condemnation
as though it were a sour but precious fruit. He torments
himself perversely as long as he does not realize that precisely
in this disillusionment and doubt and despair Christ is
thrusting into his life to free him from the bonds of self.
But how shall we show him that it is none other than the
grip of Christ under which he suffers, and that this painful
grip is aiming to free him from his tormented self? Is this
the touch of Christ?" he will ask, and we shall counter by
asking him, "How can it not be?" If you are honest with
yourself, can you ever free yourself from this word which has
pierced your life like a sword, and from this experience which
has intruded upon it with disturbing force? Does it not
awaken in you an unceasing unrest, as it awakens unrest in
the world at large which can never be again as it once was,
before the word and message of Christ resounded in it? in
the world which again to-day is so obviously striving to
resist the thrust of Christ who wishes to shatter its pride and
so free it from its torment? Is not your dispeace due precisely
to this-that you have encountered the disturbing force of
the word of Christ, so that you are driven to confess: "It was
easier and would be easier without this intrusive touch"?
"Were it not for this intrusive word, then life might be
mastered, for then it would be a closed and secure circle"?
Do you look back with nostalgic regret to the time before
this strange disturbance, as we look back with longing to the
time of childhood? Now in this very state of mind you must
and may realize that you are being gripped by the saving
